findings.title: Index created without CONCURRENTLY locks writes on a large table
findings.explanation: A plain CREATE INDEX takes a SHARE lock on `events`, blocking all INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE for the duration of the build. The events table is likely large and write-heavy (activity feed), so this can cause an outage or request pile-up during deploy. Use `CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY IF NOT EXISTS ...`. Note that CONCURRENTLY cannot run inside a transaction block, so make sure the migration runner does not wrap this file in a transaction (or configure it to run this migration outside one). Also be aware that a failed concurrent build leaves an INVALID index that must be dropped before retrying.

findings.title: Not idempotent; no IF NOT EXISTS
findings.explanation: If the migration is partially applied, re-run, or the index was already created manually in production (common when hot-fixing performance), the migration will fail with 'relation already exists'. Use `IF NOT EXISTS` to make it safe to re-run.

findings.title: No evidence the index matches the actual query or is used
findings.explanation: The PR claims the query does a sequential scan, but the query itself and an EXPLAIN (ANALYZE) before/after are not included. Please confirm the endpoint orders by `id DESC` filtered by `project_id` (and uses keyset pagination on `id`), and that any extra filters (e.g. event type, created_at) are covered. Otherwise the index may not be used. Also check for an existing index on `project_id` that this would make redundant (extra write overhead and storage).

findings.title: Consider explicit DESC necessity and rollback note
findings.explanation: Postgres can scan a (project_id, id) btree backwards, so `id DESC` is not strictly required unless mixed-direction ordering is used. It is harmless, but a short comment on the intent and a down/rollback migration (`DROP INDEX CONCURRENTLY IF EXISTS events_project_id_idx`) would help future maintainers.

## Speed up the project activity feed

The project events endpoint does a sequential scan per project. Adds an index on `events (project_id, id DESC)` to match the query.

## Diff

```diff

new file mode 100644
index 0000000..0586576
--- /dev/null
+++ b/migrations/005_events_project_idx.sql
@@ -0,0 +1 @@
+CREATE INDEX events_project_id_idx ON events (project_id, id DESC);
```
